models.rule: Only top-tier models. Effort defaults to high and never drops below medium.
models.effortNote: agy accepts --effort only for Gemini. Claude models think at a fixed level; GPT-OSS has effort in its slug.

accounts.label: Account 2
accounts.note: Disabled until verified. The CLI sign-in is not stored in the profile folder, so a second CLI account needs a tested switch first. Until then, account 2 runs Antigravity Desktop.

accounts.label: Antigravity Desktop
accounts.note: Not scriptable. It takes tickets assigned to @agy-desktop from the board.

budget.note: Worker tokens per day across all accounts. Claude Code's own usage is shown but not capped here.

notify.note: Set ntfyTopic to a private random name and install the ntfy app to get these on your phone.

schedules.label: Morning standup
schedules.note: Built from the event log. No model runs, no tokens.

ticket.title: MedPark weekly speed check
ticket.description: Run PageSpeed Insights (mobile) on https://www.medparkhospitals.com/, /medparkhospital.php, /healthhub.php, /contact-us/ and /pl/. Record performance score and LCP per page as a note, compared with the last check in this ticket history. Read only: do not change any file or server.
acceptance: One line per page: score and LCP
Any page that got worse is named first

schedules.label: Nightly site watchdog
schedules.note: Crawls every enabled site in watchdog.sites, confirms each fault with a second request, groups by kind, and files only what is new. A clean run is silent.

review.note: When a worker marks a ticket ready for review, a different best model reviews it first and writes notes. Uses tokens; the daily budget still applies.

policy.note: Who does a ticket when no assignee is given. First matching rule wins. Edit in Settings, with node hive/cli.js policy, or here.

specGate.note: A ticket with an epic will not dispatch until specs/<epic>/spec.md says Status: approved. Set by the head after the user approves. Small tickets carry no epic and are never gated.

rules.label: Specs are written by the head with the user
rules.why: A spec decides what gets built. The head writes it with the user and the user approves it. No worker writes a spec.

rules.label: Critical goes to the head
rules.why: Critical: a live site, money, patient safety or security. The head does it.

rules.label: Live systems go to the head
rules.why: Touches a live system or search visibility. The head does it, or a worker prepares it and the head ships it.

rules.label: Medical, price and accreditation claims go to the head
rules.why: Medical or commercial claims carry liability. The head writes or approves every word.

rules.label: Hard, high-priority code goes to the head
rules.why: High-priority logic where a subtle bug is costly.

rules.label: Visual work goes to a worker
rules.why: Visual work: Gemini 3.1 Pro handles it well and it saves the head for review.

rules.label: Volume work goes to a worker
rules.why: Reading, measuring, converting or drafting in bulk. A worker does it; the head reviews.

rules.label: Everything else goes to a worker
rules.why: Default: a worker does it, the head reviews and merges.

consult.note: Read-only questions to agy (the /delegate pattern). Sandboxed: can read, never write.

watchdog.note: Domains the nightly watchdog crawls. Add, remove or set enabled:false here. No code change needed. Medcierge is deliberately absent: the project is closed until the user reopens it.
